name: Lienzer Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The historic old town of Lienz enchants as a sunny Dolomite town with Schloss Liebburg, a Mediterranean main square, and views of the Isel River.
tags: Leinz (or 'Lienz' if referring to the city)
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic old town of Lienz – the sun-drenched district capital of East Tyrol at 673 metres above sea level – impresses with its distinctive Mediterranean flair at the confluence of the Isel and Drau rivers. Framed by the rugged limestone towers of the Lienzer Dolomiten, the traffic-calmed town centre enchants locals and visitors with colourful townhouse facades, bustling pavement cafes shaded by palm trees, and more than 750 years of history as a former trading and residential hub of the Counts of Gorizia (Görz).

History & Sights

Lienz was granted municipal rights in 1242 by Count Meinhard III of Gorizia. Following the extinction of the Gorizian dynasty in 1500, the town passed to Emperor Maximilian I and thereby to the County of Tyrol. The architectural centerpiece of the spacious main square (Hauptplatz) is the stately Schloss Liebburg: built in the early 17th century by the Barons of Wolkenstein-Rodenegg as a residential castle with its two prominent onion-domed towers, it now serves as the town's majestic town hall. Right alongside, the baroque St.-Antonius-Kirchlein offers a quiet retreat for contemplation. Other sacred treasures include the gothic Franciscan Monastery on the banks of the Isel with precious 15th-century wall paintings and the three-aisled parish church of St. Andrä featuring late-Gothic funerary monuments of the Counts of Gorizia. Every Friday and Saturday, the Messinggasse area transforms into the traditional Lienz City Market, where mountain farmers from across East Tyrol offer regional culinary specialities.

Visit & Arrival

The pedestrian zone of Lienz's historic old town is freely accessible 24 hours a day, all year round, and completely free of charge. The boutiques, specialist shops, and galleries are generally open Monday through Friday from 09:00 to 18:00 and Saturdays from 09:00 to 17:00. In summer, open-air concerts and cultural events regularly grace the Hauptplatz. Arrival by rail: Lienz railway station is a major transport junction of the ÖBB (regional S-Bahn and REX connections from Spittal an der Drau and Innichen/San Candido in South Tyrol); from the station forecourt, it is just a three-minute stroll across the Isel bridge directly into the Hauptplatz. By car: Via the Drautal road B100 or the Felbertauern road B108 directly to Lienz; parking options surround the old town (e.g. Parkgarage Zentrum or Dolomitencenter car park).

Tips

The entire town centre is car-free and, thanks to flat stone paving, perfectly accessible with strollers and wheelchairs. In summer, savour homemade gelato at one of the pavement cafes on the main square with clear views of the Lienzer Dolomiten. From Johannesplatz, a picturesque walking path along the Isel promenade leads directly to the confluence of the Isel and Drau.
